question.q: We still run a non-CDB 19c database. Does that matter for the Azure move?
question.expected: Non-CDB architecture is desupported in 21c (deprecated 12.1); any lift to 21c/23ai on Azure VMs or Oracle Database@Azure requires converting to a PDB first; irrelevant for SQL MI/PostgreSQL targets except as an upgrade prerequisite.

passages.text: 11.2, 12.1, 12.2, 18c, 19c | M | workaround | Exadata Database Service, which underpins Oracle Database@Azure, creates databases from the console and APIs only as container databases with an initial pluggable database. A non-CDB can be created only through the dbaascli command line and only for release 19.x and earlier, so a non-CDB estate should be converted to PDBs (AutoUpgrade does this in one step) before or during the move rather than preserved. | Inventory non-CDB databases and their release. Create a target CDB on the Exadata VM cluster from the Azure portal and OCI console. Use AutoUpgrade or Data Pump to upgrade and plug each non-CDB in as a PDB. Reserve dbaascli non-CDB creation for temporary 19c compatibility only.

11.2, 12.1, 12.2, 18c, 19c | M | workaround | On a self-managed VM any Oracle release can be installed, so a 19c non-CDB can be lifted as-is, but that only postpones the conversion because later releases are multitenant-only. AutoUpgrade can upgrade and convert a non-CDB into a PDB of a new or existing CDB in a single operation, which is the recommended step when moving to a VM on a newer release. | Provision the VM with the target Oracle release from the marketplace image or a custom image. Create an empty CDB on the VM. Run AutoUpgrade with the non-CDB as source and the CDB as target to upgrade and plug in. Update connection strings to the PDB service name.

Oracle Database 21c Upgrade Guide | States that the non-CDB architecture is desupported from 21c, that a CDB is the only supported architecture, and that a non-CDB must be upgraded by plugging it into a CDB as a PDB. | oracle | 2026-09-26 | Oracle Database Upgrade Guide 21c: Manual Non-CDB Oracle Database Release Upgrades to Multitenant Architecture | https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/21/upgrd/upgrade-scenarios-non-cdb-oracle-databases.html

11.2, 12.1, 12.2, 18c, 19c, 21c, 23ai | M | partial | Azure SQL Database has no Agent, so legacy DBMS_JOB submissions become Elastic Jobs: T-SQL steps run by a separate job agent against one or more databases on a UTC schedule. Simple interval jobs map cleanly; jobs that expected to run inside the same database engine with the submitter's transaction semantics, or that called OS-level code, do not. | Provision an elastic job agent with a dedicated, non-Hyperscale job database. Convert each job's PL/SQL body to a stored procedure in the target database. Define a target group for the database(s) and a job with a T-SQL step that executes the procedure. Translate the Oracle INTERVAL expression to a schedule, remembering all times are UTC. Make the step idempotent, because the agent retries failed executions.

removed, discontinued | Oracle's status for a feature it no longer fixes bugs for and whose code it may have removed from the product. A desupported feature can fail or vanish after an upgrade, so any target that runs a newer Oracle release (for example Oracle Database@Azure on 26ai) forces a replacement before or during the move, and a non-Oracle target needs a functional equivalent regardless. Contrast with deprecated, where the feature still works and is still supported. | Desupported

multitenant architecture, container database, pluggable database | A container database (CDB) is one Oracle database that hosts a root container (CDB$ROOT) holding Oracle-supplied metadata and common users, a seed template (PDB$SEED) used to stamp out new containers, and zero or more pluggable databases. A pluggable database (PDB) is a portable set of schemas and objects that looks like a standalone database to applications and can be unplugged and plugged into another CDB. A non-CDB is the pre-multitenant single-database architecture, deprecated in 12.1 and desupported in 21c, so every current Oracle target is a CDB and a migrated non-CDB has to land as a PDB. On Oracle Database@Azure some CDB and PDB management tasks are done in the OCI console rather than the Azure portal. | CDB / PDB / non-CDB

Treat every 'converted' autonomous transaction as a manual rewrite when the target is Managed Instance or Azure SQL Database. Typical replacements: write audit rows through a separate connection from the application tier, use table variables (which survive a rollback) to carry log data out of the failing transaction, or move the side effect to a Service Broker activation procedure on Managed Instance. Verify by searching the converted T-SQL for xp_ora2ms_exec2_ex before deploying. | Does SSMA's autonomous-transaction emulation run on Managed Instance? | SSMA reports PRAGMA AUTONOMOUS_TRANSACTION in procedures and functions as converted, because it emulates the pragma with an extended stored procedure that opens a second connection. Microsoft's own list of T-SQL differences says Azure SQL Managed Instance does not support extended stored procedures at all. One Microsoft tool marks as done what another Microsoft platform cannot host.

platform | 12.1 | 21c | pre-11.2 | Non-CDB architecture | Multitenant architecture (CDB with pluggable databases) | A non-CDB is a database created in the classic single-database layout, where one instance owns one data dictionary and one set of user schemas with no container root and no pluggable databases. The multitenant architecture, introduced in 12.1, adds a root container and pluggable databases (PDBs) that can be unplugged, cloned and moved. Migrations care because a large share of the estates being moved to Azure are 11.2 and 12.x non-CDBs. The architecture changes what assessment tools see (there is no PDB scoping), how users and services are structured (no common users or per-PDB services), and whether the source can be upgraded in place to a release that current migration tooling supports before the move. Oracle's 12.1 Upgrade Guide lists the non-CDB architecture as deprecated, and the 12.2 guide repeats the deprecation. The 21c Upgrade Guide desupports it (notice dated May 2021): the installer can no longer create a non-CDB, and upgrading to 21c or later requires converting the database into a PDB.

result:
**Yes, it matters.** The non-CDB layout is desupported from 21c onward, so if you move to Oracle Database@Azure you'll have to convert it to a pluggable database (PDB). On an Azure VM you can keep it for now, but that only puts the conversion off.

**Why it matters**
- Oracle deprecated the non-CDB architecture in 12.1 and desupported it in 21c. From 21c the installer can't create a non-CDB, and upgrading to 21c or later means converting it into a PDB. [3][6][8]
- Every current Oracle target is a container database (CDB), so a migrated non-CDB has to become a PDB. [6]

**If the target is Oracle Database@Azure (Exadata Database Service)**
- The console and APIs only create CDBs with an initial PDB. You can create a non-CDB only through the `dbaascli` command line, and only for 19.x and earlier. [1]
- Recommendation: create a target CDB on the Exadata VM cluster, then use AutoUpgrade or Data Pump to upgrade and plug each non-CDB in as a PDB. Use `dbaascli` to create a non-CDB only if you need temporary 19c compatibility. [1]
- Some CDB and PDB management tasks are done in the OCI console rather than the Azure portal. [6]

**If the target is a self-managed Azure VM**
- You can install any release there, so you can move the 19c non-CDB as it is. Later releases are multitenant-only, though, so you'll still have to convert eventually. [2]
- If you're moving to a newer release on the VM, the recommended route is:
  1. Create an empty CDB on the VM.
  2. Run AutoUpgrade with the non-CDB as the source and the CDB as the target. It upgrades and plugs in the database in one operation.
  3. Change connection strings to the PDB service name. [2]

**Also plan for:** the non-CDB layout changes what assessment tools see (no PDB scoping) and how users and services are set up (no common users or per-PDB services). [8]

**Source:** Oracle Database 21c Upgrade Guide, non-CDB to multitenant upgrades: https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/21/upgrd/upgrade-scenarios-non-cdb-oracle-databases.html

Passages [4] and [7] are about Azure SQL targets and aren't relevant to this question.
